chunks: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Musa عليه السلام: "What prevents you from conversing with Me?" He said: "My Lord, I hold You too exalted for intimate conversation because of the odor of the fasting person's mouth." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "O Musa, the odor of the fasting person's mouth is more pleasant to Me than the fragrance of musk."

key_terms.أَطْيَبُ: more pleasant or sweeter in rank before Allah
key_terms.أَوْحَى: revealed; denotes divine communication from Allah
key_terms.اَلصَّائِمِ: the fasting person; one observing sawm (fasting)
key_terms.خُلُوفِ: the changed odor of the mouth caused by fasting
key_terms.رِيحِ اَلْمِسْكِ: the fragrance of musk; a comparison for a most pleasant scent
key_terms.مُنَاجَاتِي: conversing intimately with Me; private devotional discourse with Allah

ai.seo_question: Why is the odor of a fasting person's mouth considered beloved to Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the virtue of sawm (fasting) and the special nearness of the fasting person to Allah. It teaches that what may seem unpleasant outwardly, such as the altered breath of the fasting person, is honored by Allah because it results from an act of devotion.
